learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries for Long-Duration Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries store energy for over 100 hours, solving renewable intermittency. Unlike lithium-ion, they use cheap iron and ambient air, making them ideal for multi-day backup. As India scales solar and wind, long-duration storage becomes critical to ensure reliable supply during low-generation periods.
learn.c1_text: India aims for 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, requiring massive storage. The National Green Hydrogen Mission includes funding for pilot projects. IIT Madras is developing low-cost iron-air prototypes. With solar generation peaking midday but demand highest evening, 100-hour storage could transform India's grid reliability.
learn.c2_text: Iron-air batteries offer 100+ hour discharge cycles versus 4-6 hours for lithium-ion. They use abundant iron instead of scarce materials like lithium and cobalt. Costs could drop below $50/kWh. Their self-discharge rate is minimal, making them ideal for seasonal storage applications.

learn.title: Offshore Wind Farms: Design and Grid Integration
learn.intro: Offshore wind farms harness stronger, more consistent winds than land-based turbines, offering huge potential for clean energy. With water depths reaching 60+ meters and turbines now exceeding 15 MW, these installations require advanced engineering. India's 2024 offshore wind policy targets 30 GW capacity.
learn.c1_text: India's 2024 offshore wind policy targets 30 GW by 2030. The first commercial project in Tamil Nadu's Kanyakumari district will use 15 MW turbines. Challenges include monsoon resilience and cyclone resistance. The government plans 4.5 GW of offshore wind auctions, leveraging India's 7,500 km coastline for clean energy generation.
learn.c2_text: Offshore farms connect via undersea cables to onshore substations. Electricity travels through offshore substations that step up voltage to reduce transmission losses. HVDC (High Voltage Direct Current) links efficiently transport power over hundreds of kilometers. Complex coordination ensures stable grid frequency despite variable wind patterns.

learn.stat3: Turbine size: 15+ MW offshore units now available
learn.stat4: India target: 30 GW offshore wind by 2030

learn.title: Hydrogen Colors: Blue, Green, and Grey Explained
learn.intro: Hydrogen production methods determine environmental impact. Grey hydrogen from fossil fuels emits CO2, blue captures it, and green uses renewables. Understanding these distinctions is crucial as India launches its National Green Hydrogen Mission with $2.3 billion investment to become a global manufacturing hub.
learn.c1_text: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission allocates $2.3 billion to produce 5 MMT green hydrogen annually by 2030. Reliance Industries plans $70 billion investment in green hydrogen manufacturing. IOCL will set up India's first commercial green hydrogen plant in Gujarat. This aligns with India's net-zero 2070 commitment.
learn.c2_text: Green hydrogen splits water using renewable electricity via electrolysis, producing zero emissions. Currently costs $3-8/kg versus $1-2/kg for grey. However, prices are falling rapidly. It's like comparing electric cars to gasoline – higher upfront cost but cleaner operation and decreasing price advantage over time.

learn.title: Flow Batteries for Grid-Scale Energy Storage
learn.intro: Flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes, offering scalable, long-duration storage. Vanadium and iron systems can discharge for 10+ hours, unlike traditional batteries. As India adds 50 GW renewable capacity annually, grid-scale storage becomes essential for managing supply variability and ensuring grid stability.
learn.c1_text: India needs 20 GW grid-scale storage by 2030 to support renewable integration. NTPC plans India's first 10 MW vanadium flow battery project in Gujarat. The government's Production Linked Incentive scheme supports domestic battery manufacturing. With 175 GW renewable target by 2022, storage is critical for evening peak management.
learn.c2_text: Flow batteries separate power (stack size) from energy (tank size). Doubling storage means adding larger tanks, not duplicating entire systems. This enables 10-100+ hour discharge cycles. Unlike lithium-ion which degrades after 4-6 hours, flow batteries maintain performance for decades with minimal capacity loss.

learn.stat2: Flow battery duration: 10-100+ hour discharge cycles

learn.title: Solar PV Panels: Photoelectric Effect Explained
learn.intro: Solar PV panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect – a phenomenon Einstein won a Nobel Prize for. With India installing 15 GW solar annually and achieving grid parity, understanding this technology's physics helps appreciate why solar is now the world's cheapest electricity source.
learn.c1_text: India's Bhadla Solar Park spans 14,000 acres with 2.2 GW capacity – world's largest. The country added 10.5 GW solar in 2023, reaching 75 GW total. Solar tariffs hit ₹1.96/kWh in 2020, cheaper than coal. The International Solar Alliance, headquartered in India, coordinates 121 countries for global solar deployment.
learn.c2_text: Individual cells produce ~0.5 volts DC. Panels connect multiple cells in series/parallel to increase voltage/current. Inverters convert DC to AC for homes. Anti-reflective coatings boost efficiency by reducing photon reflection. Modern panels achieve 20-22% efficiency, meaning 20-22% of sunlight becomes usable electricity.
learn.stat2: Bhadla Solar Park: 2.2 GW capacity across 14,000 acres
learn.stat4: Solar panel efficiency: 20-22% for commercial panels

learn.title: Electricity Grid: Real-Time Supply-Demand Balance
learn.intro: Electricity grids must balance supply and demand every second – too much causes blackouts, too little causes brownouts. As India adds variable renewables, maintaining this balance becomes complex. Smart grids, forecasting, and fast-response storage help manage fluctuations while keeping lights on for 240 million households.
learn.c1_text: India's grid frequency varies ±0.5 Hz due to renewable fluctuations. The Green Energy Corridor project invested $2.6 billion to integrate 160 GW renewables. POSOCO operates 5 regional grids with real-time monitoring. India achieved 99.97% uptime in 2023 despite adding 15 GW renewable capacity annually.
learn.c2_text: AGC systems automatically adjust power plant output every few seconds based on frequency deviations. When demand spikes, AGC signals gas turbines to ramp up within minutes. Renewables complicate this since solar/wind can't be dispatched on command. Grid-scale batteries now provide millisecond responses to maintain stability.
